"10.1 The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to quash/ set-aside the impugned report dated 01.07.2022 (P/1) issued by the Tehsildar, Sakri, District Bilaspur, C.G. 10.2 The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondent State to grant compensation to the petitioner for the balance 0.37 acres of land.

Learned counsel for petitioner would submit that petitioner has earlier approached this Court raising grievance that initially the land, subject matter of the acquisition,
was more, however, the amount of compensation calculated is of less area of land which was acquired and used by the respondents for the purpose of construction of canal.
The writ petition was disposed of directing the SDO (R.) or the Collector, after reference of the matter by the SDO(R.) to take decision on the pending representation/ objection Annexure P-6 therein.
Pursuant thereto petitioner has again submitted fresh representation to the SDO(R.) on 19.10.2020, proceedings of which are still pending consideration.

During pendency of the proceedings, the SDO(R.) has called for the report from the Tahsildar or the Revenue Inspector concerned with respect to the land owned by the petitioner and the land acquired,
used for the purpose of construction of canal.

Earlier the Tahsildar has submitted the report mentioning that the petitioner's land measuring 1.46 Acres were used,
however, in the subsequent report submitted by the Revenue Inspector it is mentioned that the land for which the compensation is claimed measuring 0.37 Acres is lying vacant, not used for the purpose of construction of canal, it is adjacent to the Arpa Bhainsajar Project and it is in possession of petitioner also.
The report submitted by the Revenue Inspector is contrary to the earlier report of the Tahsildar and therefore the report Annexure P-1 be quashed.

3. Learned State counsel would oppose the submission of learned counsel for petitioner and would submit that from the pleadings made in the writ petition and the documents enclosed, it appears that petitioner earlier approached this Court by filing writ petition raising grievance of calculating less amount of compensation,
showing less land was acquired and used for construction of canal, however, more land was used and the amount of compensation with respect to 0.37 acres of land was not paid.

This court disposed of that writ petition directing SDO(R.) or the Collector to consider the representation submitted by the petitioner keeping in mind the provisions under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: 4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the records.

5. The petitioner along with the writ petition has filed copy of order dated 15.09.2020 passed in WPC No. 1938/2020 (Laxmi Kaushik vs. State of C.G.), perusal of which would show that the petitioner has raised same grievance that 0.80 acre of land out of 1.46 acres was used, however, the amount of compensation is paid only with respect to 0.43 acres and no amount of compensation is paid with respect to 0.37 acres

entities.text: WPC No. 1938/2020 (Laxmi Kaushik vs. State of C.G.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: . Considering the submission of learned counsel for petitioner, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court disposed of that writ petition observing that Respondent No. 3 ie., the SDO(R.) therein to take decision on the representation, Annexure P-6 therein dated 21.05.2018 within a period of 90 days.
It is further observed that if for any reason the SDO(R.) feels that he is not the competent authority then the decision is to be taken by the Collector on the reference being made by the SDO(R.).
Annexure P-13 is the fresh representation submitted by the petitioner pursuant to the order passed in writ petition.
The representation is dated 19.10.2020.

In the writ petition, petitioner has not submitted any document showing that the SDO(R.) or the Collector pursuant to the order passed by this Court has taken final decision on the claim of petitioner, however, from the argument raised and the documents placed on record it is appearing that based on the order of this Court dated 15.09.2020 in the earlier writ petition and the representation submitted by petitioner, the SDO(R.) is still considering the claim of petitioner and in that process the report was called from the concerned Revenue Inspector.

The report submitted by the Revenue Inspector is still to be considered by the SDO(R.) and to apply its mind and therefore in the opinion of this Court, this writ petition at this stage is pre-mature because the competent authority has not taken any decision on the report, and not finalize the proceedings.
6. Accordingly the writ petition is dismissed.

However, the petitioner will be at liberty to take recourse of law against the final decision of the SDO(R.) or the Collector who has to pass the order on the representation submitted by petitioner based on the earlier order passed by this Court in WPC No. 1938/2020 dated 15.09.2020.
